message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thrillers released (or widely available) in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|------------------|
| 1 | **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki | A mind‑bending heist thriller that blends time‑travel mechanics with high‑stakes espionage. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie's signature fast‑paced dialogue and stylish visuals make this a sharp, comedic take on drug‑dealership turf wars. |
| 3 | **Uncut Gems** | Josh & Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett, Jennifer Lawrence | Sandler’s manic performance anchors a tense narrative about risk, addiction, and desperation. |
| 4 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Though released on Netflix in 2019, it dominated 2020 discussions; its epic scope and de-aging tech give it a unique place in modern crime cinema. |
| 5 | **The Night Clerk** | Daniel Kwan & Daniel Scheinert (the Daniels) | Ben Affleck, Lily James | A darkly comic, surreal take on a night‑shift clerk who becomes entangled in a murder mystery. |
| 6 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A Danish film that uses a small-town setting to explore paranoia, betrayal, and moral ambiguity. |
| 7 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A psychological thriller that reimagines the classic horror premise as a story about abuse and gaslighting. |
| 8 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | While more courtroom drama than traditional crime‑thriller, its tense pacing and historical stakes earn it a spot here. |
| 9 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned political intrigue, blending period detail with a gripping narrative. |
|10 | **The Platform** | Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Iván Massagué, Zorion Eguileor | A Spanish allegory that turns a vertical prison into a claustrophobic thriller about class and survival. |

These films cover a range of styles—from slick action and satire to gritty realism and psychological suspense—making them worth checking out if you’re looking for top-tier crime‑thrillers from 2020.
